game_info.title: Starship Troopers
game_info.based_on: Starship Troopers by Robert A. Heinlein (1959)
game_info.map: Hex-based, 3-section board-mounted map, each hex = 1 mile across

turn_sequence.description: The game is played in turns. Each turn consists of player segments for Terran/Humanoid and Arachnid forces.

phases.name: Player Segment Special Function
phases.description: Initiate special placement and detonation procedures

phases.name: Movement Phase
phases.description: Terran player moves non-samoloid unit counters up to their movement allowance

phases.name: Range Weapon Phase
phases.description: Terran player initiates and resolves attacks against enemy units within range of special weapons units

phases.name: Close Combat Phase
phases.description: Terran player initiates and resolves attacks against enemy units in the same hex

phases.name: Extended Jump Phase
phases.description: Terran player moves mobile infantry units again up to half their normal movement allowance

phases.name: Tunnel Service Movement
phases.description: Arachnid player moves underground units and conducts special construction/demolition procedures

phases.name: Range Weapon Phase
phases.description: Arachnid player initiates and resolves attacks against enemy units within range of ranged heavy weapons

phases.name: Movement Phase
phases.description: Arachnid player moves all units including engineers to the limits of their movement allowances

phases.name: Close Combat Phase
phases.description: Arachnid player initiates and resolves attacks against enemy units in the same hex with friendly Warrior units

combat_resolution.description: Combat resolution centers on comparing total attack factors against defense factors to generate odds ratios
steps: Sum total attack strength points of all attacking units
Sum total defense strength points of all defending units
Express the two totals as an odds ratio (Attacker:Defender)
Round off the odds ratio downwards to conform to simplified odds categories
Roll one six-sided die on the appropriate attack table
Apply the result to the target unit(s)

outcomes.miss: No effect - attack fails to hit target
outcomes.disrupted: Target may not move, re-enter tunnel systems, or engage in any type of attack during the next player segment. Place disrupted marker on unit. Remove marker at end of next player segment.
outcomes.wia: Wounded in Action - Target unit is wounded and has reduced effectiveness
outcomes.kia: Killed in Action - Target unit is destroyed and eliminated as a combat force. Remove unit from play.
outcomes.hvy: Heavy Damage - Target unit is heavily damaged with significant reduction in capabilities

attack_tables.terran_attack_table: Used when Terran units attack Arachnid or Humanoid units
attack_tables.alien_attack_table: Used when Arachnid units attack Terran units. Humanoid units use Terran attack table when defending.

movement_rules.normal_movement: Units move up to their movement allowance in hexes per phase
movement_rules.road_movement: Units on roads may move double their normal movement allowance
movement_rules.tunnel_movement: Arachnid units move through hidden tunnel systems underground. Tunnel movement is tracked on the Alien Control Pad.
movement_rules.breach_rules: Arachnid units surface through breaches in the terrain. Breaches are created by the Arachnid player and hidden from the Terran player.
movement_rules.stacking: Multiple units may occupy the same hex. Terran and Humanoid units may not voluntarily stack together unless involuntarily immobilized as a result of combat.

special_rules.line_of_sight: Units must have line of sight to their targets. Terrain features block LOS.
special_rules.suppression: Heavy weapons can suppress enemy units, reducing their effectiveness
special_rules.nuclear_weapons: Nuclear demolition munitions can be used but have area effects on friendly units
special_rules.sensors: Terran units can be equipped with sensors to detect underground tunnel systems
special_rules.victory_points: Victory is determined by counting victory points for eliminated units and objectives
